text:
sam: Heads up — started seeing tail-token stalls in prod at ~23:10 UTC on the tp+pp multi-GPU stack. Latency spikes only on some shards, looks like compute is idling while all-reduce holds. Suspect interaction between graph-capture replay, kernel-selector fallbacks, and KV-cache prefetching.

maya: link to flame: http://perf/trace/1234 :eyes: any obvious recent changes to kernel picker?

sam: rolled a canary back to tag abc1235 (older kernel selector) and overlap comes back. quick ncu snippet from the failing run (trimmed):

```
NVTX timeline:
[0.0ms] stream0: forward_kernels (compute)
[1.2ms] stream1: cudaGraphLaunch(replay)
[1.3ms] stream1: allreduce_start
[1.3ms] stream0: waiting (idle)
[3.8ms] cudaMemcpy (host->dev) on default stream -> serialization point
[4.0ms] allreduce_end
[4.1ms] compute resumes

Observed: host memcpy on default stream during KV warmup blocks other streams after capture replay, and kernel-selector sometimes chooses a fused kernel that forces work onto the capture stream.
```

kevin: that fits something I instrumented earlier — when batch shapes are small the selector picks the single-fused kernel (lower per-kernel overhead) but it has poorer stream-locality. With graph capture enabled, replay pins that fused kernel into the captured graph and places all subsequent launches on the capture stream -> serialization. KV prefetch does a `cudaMemcpy` without explicit stream -> ends up on default stream and triggers implicit sync after capture replay.

anya: CI perf job failed yesterday with similar symptoms: https://ci/build/789 log snippet: `cudaGraphLaunch returned error 3` intermittently. We thought it was a driver flake but the timing aligns with KV cache warmups.

sam: quick mitigation proposals:
- disable graph capture for tp+pp combos when batch_len < 16 (fast path uses runtime launch)
- ensure KV prefetch uses per-batch async stream (assign prefetch_stream and cudaMemcpyAsync into that stream)
- add kernel-selector rule: prefer split-kernel (split compute + comm-friendly kernels) when seq_len variance > 0.2 or when estimated allreduce_time > threshold

maya: can someone repro locally? if not I'll add a light-weight logging gate to kernel selector so we can see "why" it picked fused vs split: set env `KSEL_LOG=1` and it'll dump the decision factors.

sam: repro steps I used on perf node (docker/perf:latest):
```bash
# run the small repro (tp=2 pp=2, bs=8, seq_len dist skewed)
docker run --gpus all -it perf:latest /bin/bash -c '\
python perf_harness/run.py --model gpt-small --tp 2 --pp 2 --batch 8 --seq-distribution skewed --enable-cgraph=1 --kv-prefetch=1\'
```

deploy-bot: Perf job queued: job/2645007901 (tau cluster).

kevin: i'll try a quick patch: compute an `estimated_allreduce_time = dims * pp_world / comm_bw` and force non-fused when est_allreduce_time > 0.5ms (tunable). i'll run microbench against the perf harness and post numbers.

maya: also add config `CGRAPH_PREFETCH=0` to gate cgraph capture when kv_prefetch is true — easier short-term toggle for Dedicated.

anya: for SRE: if this affects dedicated customers we should consider rolling processes per node with the cgraph toggle off. i'll coordinate maintenance windows once we have repro + patch.

sam: thanks all — i'll collect the ncu traces and drop them into the perf thread. for alerting, temporarily set anomaly window to 2x on `mgpu-allreduce-latency` so we don't noisy-alert while we iterate.

maya: assigning follow-ups: @kevin to prototype selector change, @sam to add prefetch stream assignment + repro, @anya to prepare optional rollout. update this thread with links. :thumbsup:
